العبد من حين يصبح إلى حين يمسي، له نور كنور الشمس، حتى إذا صعدت به إلى
السماء الدنيا زكته وكثرته، فيقول الملك الموكل بها للحفظة: اضربوا بهذا
العمل وجه صاحبه، أنا صاحب الغيبة، أمرني ربي ألا أدع عمل من اغتاب الناس
يجاوزني إلى غيري، قال: ثم تأتي الحفظة بعمل صالح من أعمال العبد له نور
فتزكيه وتكثره حتى تبلغ به إلى السماء الثانية، فيقول لهم الملك الموكل
بها: قفوا، واضربوا بهذا العمل وجه صاحبه، إنه أرا بعمله عرض الدنيا، أنا
ملك الفخر، أمرني ربي ألا أدع عمله يجاوزني إلى غيري، إنه كان يفتخر على
الناس في مجالسهم، قال: وتصعد الحفظة بعمل العبد يبتهج نورا، من صدقة وصلا
وصيام، قد أعجب الحفظة، فيجاوزون به إلى السماء الثالثة، فيقول لهم الملك
الموكل بها: قفوا، واضربوا بهذا العمل وجه صاحبه، أنا ملك الكبر، أمرني ربي
ألا أدع عمله يجاوزني إلى غيري؛ إنه كان يتكبرى على الناس في مجالسهم، قال:
وتصعد الحفظة بعمل العبد يزهو كما يزهو الكوكب الدري وله دوي من تسبيح
وصلاة وصيام وحج وعمرة، حتى يجاوزا به إلى السماء الرابعة، فيقول لهم الملك
الموكل بها: قفوا، واضربوا
بهذا العمل وجه صاحبه وظهره  وبطنه، أنا صاحب العجب، أمرني ربي ألا أدع
عمله يجاوزني إلى غيري؛ إنه كان إذا عمل عملا أدخل العجب فيه، قال: وتصعد
الحفظة بعمل العب حتى يجاوزا به إلى السماء الخامسة كأنه العروس المزفوفة
إلى بعلها، فيقول الملك الموكل بها: قفوا واضربوا بهذا العمل وجه صاحبه، ن
واحملوه على عاتقه، أنا ملك الحسد، إنه كان يحسد من يتعلم ويعمل بمثل عمله،
وكل من كان يأخذ فضلا من العبادة كان يحسدهم، ويقع فيهم، أمرني ربي ألا أدع
عمله يجاوزني إلى غيري.
قال: وتصعد الحفظة بعمل العبد له ضوء كضوء الشمس، من صلاة وزكاة وحج
وعمرة وجهاد وصيام، فيجاوزون به إلى السماء السادسة، فيقول لهم الملك
الموكل بها: قفوا واضربوا بهذا العمل وجه صاحبه؛ إنه كان لا يرحم إنسانا قد
من عباد الله أصابه بلاء أو مرض، بل كان يشمت به، أنا ملك الرحمة، أمرني
ربي ألا أدع عمله يجاوزني إلى غيري، قال: وتصعد الحفظة بعمل العبد من صوم
وصلاة ونفقة وجهاد وورع، له دوي كدوى النحل، وضوء كضوء الشمس، ومعه ثلاثة
آلاف ملك، فيجاوزون به إلى السماء السابعة، فيقول لهم الملك الموكل بها:
قفوا، واضربوا بهذا العمل وجه صاحبه، واضربوا جوارحه واقفلوا به على قلبه،
أنا صاحب الذكر، فإني أحجب عن ربي كل عمل لم يرد به وجه ربي؛ إنه إنما أراد
بعمله غير الله تعالى، إنه أراد به رفعة عند الفقهاء، وذكرا عند العلماء،
وصيتا في المدائن، أمرني ربي ألا أدع عمله يجاوزني إلى غيري وكل عمل لم يكن
لله تعالى خالصا فهو رياء، ولا يقبل الله عمل المرائي.. قال: وتصعد الحفظة
بعمل العبد من صلاة وزكاة وصيام وحج وعمرة وخلق حسن وصمت وذكر الله تعالى،
فتشيعه ملائكة السموات السبع حتى يقطعوا به الحجب كلها إلى الله تعالى،
فتشيعه ملائكة السموات السبع حتى يقطعوا به الحجب كلها إلى الله تعالى،
فيقفون بين يديه، ويشهدون له بالعمل الصالح المخلص لله تعالى، فيقول الله
تعالى: أنتم الحفظة على عمل عبدي، وأنا الرقيب  على ما في قلبه؛ إنه لم
يردني بهذا العمل، وإنما أراد به غيري، فعليه لعنتي، فتقول الملائكة كلها:
عليه لعنتك ولعنتنا، فتلعنه السموات السبع ومن فيهن) ثم بكى معاذ، وانتحب
انتحابا شديدا، وقال معاذ: قلت يا رسول الله أنت رسول الله وأنا معا، فكيف
لي بالنجاة والخلاص من ذلك؟ قال: (اقتد بي وإن كان في عملك نقص، يا معاذ
حافظ على لسانك من الوقيعة في إخوانك من حملة القرآن خاصة، واحمل ذنوبك
عليك، ولا تحملها عليهم، ولا تزل نفسك بذمهم، ولا ترفع نفسك عليهم، ولا
تدخل عمل الدنيا في عمل الآخرة، ولا تراء بعملك، ولا تتكبر في مجلسك، لكي
يحذر الناس من سوء خلقك، ولا تناج رجلا وعندك آخر، ولا تتعظم على الناس
فتنقطع عنك خيرات الدنيا والآخرة، ولا تمزق الناس بلسانك فتمزقك كلاب النار
يوم القيامة في النار، قال الله تعالى: (والناشطات نشطا) ، هل تدري من هن
يا معاذ؟، قلت: ما هن - بأبي أنت وأمي - يا رسول الله؟ قال: (كلاب في النار
تنشط اللحم من العظم) ، قلت: بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله، من يطيق هذه
الخصال ونمن ينجو منها؟ قال: (يا معاذ إنه ليسير على من يسره الله تعالى
عليه، إنما يكفيك من ذلك أن تحب للناس ما تحب لنفسك، وتكره لهم ما تكره
لنفسك، فإذن أنت يا معاذ قد سلمت) . قال خالد بن معدان: فما رأيت أحدا أكثر
تلاوة للقرآن العظيم من معاذ لهذا الحديث العظيم.
فتأمل أيها الراغب في العلم هذه الخصال، واعلم أن أعظم الاسباب في رسوخ
هذه الخبائث في القلب: طلب العلم لأجل المباهاة والمنافسة، فالعامي بمعزل
عن اكثر هذه الخصال، والمتفقه مستهدف لها، وهو متعرض للهلاك بسببها؛ فانظر
آي أمورك أهم، أتتعلم كيفية الحذر من هذه المهلكات، وتشتغل بإصلاح قلبك
وعمارة آخرتك؟ أم الأهم أن تخوض مع الخائضين، فتطلب من العلم ما هو سبب
زيارة الكبر والرياء والحسد والعجب، حتى تهلك مع الهالكين.
واعلم أن هذه الخصال
الثلاث من أمهات خبائث القلب، ولها  مغرس واحد، وهو حب الدنياي ولذلك قال
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: (حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة) ، ومع هذا فالدنيا
مزرعة للآخرة فمن أخذ من الدنيا بقدر الضرورة، ليستعين بها على الآخرة،
فالدنيا مزرعته؛ ومن أراد الدنيا ليتنعم بها، فالدنيا مهلكته.
فهذه نبذة يسيرة من ظاهر علم التقوى، وهي بداية الهداية، فإن جربت بها
نفسك وطاوعتك عليها، فعليك بكتاب (إحياء علوم الدين) لتعرف كيفية الوصول
إلى باطن التقوى.
وإن كنت تطلب العلم من القيل والقال، والمراء والجدال، فما أعظم مصيبتك
وما أطول تعبك وما أعظم حرمانك وخسرانك! فاعمل ما شئت؛ فإن الدينا التي
تطلبها بالدين لا تسلم لك، والآخرة تسلب منك؛ ن فمن طلب الدنيا بالدين
خسرهما جميعا، ومن ترك الدنيا للدين ربحهما جميعا.
فإذا عمرت بالتقوى باطن قلبك، فعند ذلك ترتفع الحجب بينك وبين ربك،
وتنكشف لك أنوار المعارف، وتنفجر من قلبك ينابيع الحكم، وتتضح لك أسرار
الملك والملكة، ويتسير لك من العلوم ما تستحقر به هذه العلوم المحدثة التي
لم يكن لها ذكر في زمن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم والتابعين.
فهذه جمل الهداية إلى بداية الطريق في معاملتك مع الله تعالى بأداء
أوامره واجتناب نواهيه، وأشير عليك الآن بجمل من الآداب لتؤاخذ نفسك بها في
مخالطتك مع عباد الله تعالى وصحبتك معهم في الدنيا.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-س-د (ḥ-s-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Envy — the desire that another's blessing be removed, accompanied by grief at their good fortune.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A moral disease of the soul opposing contentment with divine decree (riḍā bil-qadar); it is blameworthy when it spurs hostility, though the root inclination is innate.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the state of wishing deprivation upon another; metaphorical (majāz) — the "biting" of the soul, as envy "eats" good deeds like fire eats wood.
- Root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Magnitude, greatness; in moral context, arrogance — viewing oneself as greater than others.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Pride (kibr) is the soul's swelling against truth and contempt for creation; its opposite is humility (tawāḍuʿ), a station of the prophets.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical or quantitative greatness; metaphorical — the heart's haughtiness that refuses submission to truth.
- Root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Seeing, showing; riyāʾ is displaying one's deeds for others' observation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ostentation — performing worship for the gaze of creatures rather than the Creator; it nullifies sincerity (ikhlāṣ) and is a form of hidden shirk.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — visual perception; metaphorical — the act of "showing off" (murāʾāh), where the doer makes his deed a spectacle.
- Root: ع-ج-ب (ʿ-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wonder, amazement; ʿujb is self-admiration — being pleased with one's own deeds.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Self-admiration — attributing one's obedience to one's own merit rather than divine grace; it precedes pride and blinds one to one's faults.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — astonishment at something extraordinary; metaphorical — the heart's complacency with its own virtue, a subtle veil from Allah.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and circumstantial clauses (jumal shartiyyah wa ḥāliyyah) — The hadith employs repeated conditional structures ("if you guard it... if you neglect it") and circumstantial descriptions (ḥāl) of the angels' ascent, requiring careful tracking of the apodosis and the vivid narrative sequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: The reports concerning envy, pride, ostentation, and self-admiration are numerous. Sufficient for you among them is a single comprehensive hadith. For Ibn al-Mubārak narrated with his chain of transmission from a man who said to Muʿādh: "O Muʿādh, relate to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him." He said: "Then Muʿādh wept until I thought he would not stop. Then he fell silent, and then said: 'How I yearn for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and for his meeting!' Then he said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say to me: "O Muʿādh, I shall relate to you a hadith — if you guard it, it will benefit you with Allah; but if you neglect it and fail to preserve it, your proof will be cut off before Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection. O Muʿādh, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created seven angels before He created the heavens and the earth. He made for each of the seven heavens a guarding angel at its gate. The recording angels (ḥafażah) ascend with the deed of the servant from morning until evening, having a light like the light of the sun. When they ascend with it to the lowest heaven, they purify it and multiply it. Then the angel entrusted with that heaven says to the recording angels: 'Strike this deed against the face of its owner! I am the angel of backbiting (ghībah). My Lord commanded me not to let the deed of one who backbit people pass beyond me to another.'"

"He said: 'Then the recording angels come with a righteous deed from the servant's deeds, having light, and they purify it and multiply it until they reach the second heaven. The angel entrusted with it says to them: "Stop! Strike this deed against the face of its owner! He showed off his deed for the goods of this world (ʿaraḍ al-dunyā). I am the angel of vainglory (fakhr). My Lord commanded me not to let his deed pass beyond me to another — for he used to boast over people in their gatherings."'"

"He said: 'And the recording angels ascend with the servant's deed, rejoicing in its light — from charity, prayer, and fasting — and it amazes the recording angels. They pass with it to the third heaven. The angel entrusted with it says to them: "Stop! Strike this deed against the face of its owner! I am the angel of pride (kibr). My Lord commanded me not to let his deed pass beyond me to another — for he used to behave arrogantly toward people in their gatherings."'"

"He said: 'And the recording angels ascend with the servant's deed, radiant as the radiant planet (kawkab durrī) shines, having a humming sound from glorification, prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, and lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah), until they pass with it to the fourth heaven. The angel entrusted with it says to them: "Stop! Strike this deed against the face of its owner, his back, and his belly! I am the angel of self-admiration (ʿujb). My Lord commanded me not to let his deed pass beyond me to another — for whenever he performed a deed, he infused self-admiration into it."'"

"He said: 'And the recording angels ascend with the servant's deed until they pass with it to the fifth heaven, like a bride adorned and presented to her husband. The angel entrusted with it says: "Stop! Strike this deed against the face of its owner, and load it upon his shoulder! I am the angel of envy (ḥasad). For he used to envy those who learned and acted upon the like of his deed, and everyone who took excellence in worship — he envied them and slandered them. My Lord commanded me not to let his deed pass beyond me to another."'"

"He said: 'And the recording angels ascend with the servant's deed, having a radiance like the radiance of the sun — from prayer, alms (zakāh), pilgrimage, lesser pilgrimage, striving (jihād), and fasting. They pass with it to the sixth heaven. The angel entrusted with it says to them: "Stop! Strike this deed against the face of its owner! For he did not have mercy on any person among the servants of Allah afflicted by calamity or illness; rather, he gloated over him. I am the angel of mercy (raḥmah). My Lord commanded me not to let his deed pass beyond me to another."'"

"He said: 'And the recording angels ascend with the servant's deed — from fasting, prayer, expenditure, striving, and scrupulousness (waraʿ) — having a humming like the humming of bees, and a radiance like the radiance of the sun, accompanied by three thousand angels. They pass with it to the seventh heaven. The angel entrusted with it says to them: "Stop! Strike this deed against the face of its owner, strike his limbs, and seal his heart with it! I am the angel of intention (dhikr). For I veil from my Lord every deed by which His Face was not intended. He intended by his deed other than Allah the Exalted — he sought by it elevation among the jurists, mention among the scholars, and fame in the cities. My Lord commanded me not to let his deed pass beyond me to another. And every deed not purely for Allah the Exalted is ostentation (riyāʾ), and Allah does not accept the deed of the ostentatious one."'"

"He said: 'And the recording angels ascend with the servant's deed — from prayer, alms, fasting, pilgrimage, lesser pilgrimage, good character, silence, and remembrance of Allah the Exalted — and the angels of the seven heavens escort it until they pierce with it all the veils to Allah the Exalted. They stand before Him and bear witness for him to the righteous deed sincerely performed for Allah the Exalted. Then Allah the Exalted says: "You are the recording angels over My servant's deed, and I am the Watcher over what is in his heart. He did not intend Me by this deed; rather, he intended other than Me by it. Upon him be My curse." Then all the angels say: "Upon him be Your curse and our curse." So the seven heavens and all within them curse him.'"

"Then Muʿādh wept and sobbed with intense sobbing. Muʿādh said: 'I said: O Messenger of Allah, you are the Messenger of Allah and I am with you — how can I attain deliverance and salvation from that?' He said: 'Follow me, even if your deed has deficiency. O Muʿādh, guard your tongue from slandering your brothers, especially the bearers of the Qurʾān. Bear your own sins upon yourself, and do not bear them upon others. Do not lower yourself by disparaging them, nor raise yourself above them. Do not mix the works of this world into the works of the Hereafter. Do not show off with your deed, and do not act arrogantly in your gathering, lest people be wary of your bad character. Do not privately converse with a man while another is present with you. Do not magnify yourself over people, lest the goods of this world and the Hereafter be cut off from you. Do not tear people apart with your tongue, lest the dogs of Hellfire tear you apart on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire. Allah the Exalted said: {«وَالنَّاشِطَاتِ نَشْطًا»} — "By those that drag forth violently" — do you know who they are, O Muʿādh?' I said: 'What are they — may my father and mother be your ransom — O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Dogs in the Fire that tear the flesh from the bone.' I said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah — who can bear these qualities, and who can be saved from them?' He said: 'O Muʿādh, it is indeed easy for the one for whom Allah the Exalted makes it easy. It suffices you of that to love for people what you love for yourself, and to dislike for them what you dislike for yourself. Then, O Muʿādh, you have been saved.'"

Khālid ibn Maʿdān said: "I never saw anyone who recited the Mighty Qurʾān more than Muʿādh, because of this mighty hadith."

So reflect, O seeker of knowledge, upon these qualities, and know that the greatest cause of the rooting of these impurities in the heart is seeking knowledge for the sake of boasting and rivalry. The common man is remote from most of these qualities, while the jurist (mutafaqqih) is their target, exposed to destruction because of them. So consider which of your affairs is more important: do you learn how to guard against these destroyers, and occupy yourself with reforming your heart and building your Hereafter? Or is it more important to wade with those who wade, seeking from knowledge that which is a cause of increasing pride, ostentation, envy, and self-admiration, until you perish with those who perish?

Know that these qualities are among the chief impurities of the heart, and they have a single root: love of this world (ḥubb al-dunyā). For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Love of this world is the head of every sin." Yet despite this, this world is a tillage for the Hereafter. Whoever takes from this world in the measure of necessity, to aid himself thereby for the Hereafter — this world is his tillage. And whoever desires this world to indulge in its pleasures — this world is his destruction.

This, then, is a brief portion of the outward knowledge of piety (taqwā), and it is the beginning of guidance. If you have tested yourself with it and it has obeyed you therein, then you must take up the book Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn (The Revival of the Religious Sciences) to learn the manner of reaching the inward reality of piety.

But if you seek knowledge for mere talk and hearsay, for disputation and argument — how great is your affliction, how long is your toil, and how immense is your deprivation and loss! So do as you will; for this world which you seek through religion will not be secured for you, and the Hereafter will be wrested from you. Whoever seeks this world through religion loses both; and whoever abandons this world for religion gains both.

When you have built the inward of your heart with piety, then at that point the veils are lifted between you and your Lord, the lights of divine knowledge (anwār al-maʿārif) are unveiled to you, the springs of wisdom burst forth from your heart, the secrets of the dominion and the kingdom (asrār al-mulk wa al-malakūt) become clear to you, and there become easy for you sciences through which you will hold in contempt these novel sciences that had no mention in the era of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and the Followers (tābiʿūn).

These, then, are the sum of guidance to the beginning of the path in your dealing with Allah the Exalted, by performing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. And I now counsel you with a set of etiquettes (ādāb) by which you should hold yourself accountable in your mixing with the servants of Allah the Exalted and your companionship with them in this world.

chapters.title_en: The Third Section — On the Etiquette of Companionship
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القسم الثالث

القول في آداب الصحبة
آداب الصحبة مع الله تعالى اعلم أن صاحبك الذي لا يفارقك في حضرك وسفرك
ونومك ويقظتك، بل في حياتك وموتك، هو ربك وسيدك ومولاك وخالقك، ومهما ذكرته
فهو جليسك؛ إذ قال الله تعالى: (أنا جليس من ذكرين) .
ومهما انكسر قلبك حزنا على تقصيرك في حق دينك، فهو صاحبك وملازمك؛ إذ قال
الله تعالى: (أنا عند المنكسرة قلوبهم من أجلي) .
فلو عرفته حق معرفته لاتخذته صاحبا وتركت الناس جانبا. فإن لم تقدر على
ذلك في جميع أوقاتك،
فإياك أن تخلي ليلك ونهارك عن وقت تخلو فيه لمولاك وتتلذذ معه بمناجاتك
له، وعند ذلك فعليك أن تتعلم آداب الصحبة مع  الله تعالى.
وآدابها: إطراق الرأس، وغض الطرف، وجمع الهم، ودوام الصمت، وسكون
الجوارح، ومبادرة الأمر، واجتناب النهي، وقلة الاعتراض على القدر، ودوام
الذكر، وملازمة الفكر، وإيثار الحق على الباطل، والإياس عن الخلق، والخضوع
تحت الهيبة والانكسار تحت الماء، والسكون عن حيل الكسب ثقة بالضمان والتوكل
على فضل الله تعالى معرفة بحسن الاختيار.
وهذا كله ينبغي أن يكون شعارك في جميع ليلك ونهارك؛ فإنها آداب الصحبة مع
صاحب لا يفارقك، والخلق كلهم يفارقونك في بعض أوقاتك.

### | آداب العالم

وإن كنت عالما، فآداب العالم: الاحتمال، ولزوم الحلم، والجلوس بالهيبة
على سمت الوقار مع إطراق الرأس، وترك التكبر على جميع العباد إلا على
الظلمة زجرا لهم عن الظلم، وإيثارا للتواضع في المحافل والمجالس، وترك
الهزل والدعابة، والرفق بالمتعلم، والتأني بالمتعجرف، وإصلاح البليد بحسن
الارشاد، وترك الحرد عليه، وترك الأنفه من قول: (لا أدري) وصرف الهمة إلى
السائل وتفهم سؤاله، وقبول الحجة، والانقياد للحق، والرجوع إليه عند
الهفوة، ومنع المتعلم عن كل علم يضره، وزجره عن أن يريد بالعلم النافع غير
وجه الله تعالى، وصد المتعلم عن أن يشتغل بفرض الكفاية قبل الفراغ من فرض
العين.. وفرض عينه إصلاح ظاهره وباطنه بالتقوى، ومؤاخذه نفسه أولا بالتقوى
ليقتدي المتعلم أولا بأعماله، ويستفيد ثانيا من أقواله.

### | آداب المتعلم

وإن كنت متعلما، فآداب المتعلم مع العالم: أن يبدأه بالتحية والسلام، وأن
يقلل بين يديه الكلام، ولا يتكلم ما لم يسأله أستاذه، ولا يسأل ما لم
يستأذن أولا، ولا يقول في معارضة قوله: قال فلان بخلاف ما قلت، ولا يشير
عليه بخلاف رأيه فيرى أنه أعلم بالصواب من أستاذه، ولا يسأل جليسه في
مجلسه، ولا يلتفت إلى الجوانب، بل يجلس مطرقا ساكنا متآدبا كأنه في الصلاة،
ولا يكثر عليه السؤال عند ملله، وإذا قام قام له، ولا يتبعه بكلامه وسؤاله،
ولا يسأله في طريقه إلى أن يبلغ إلى منزله، ولا يسىء الظن به في أفعال
ظاهرها منكرة عنده، فهو أعلم بأسراره، وليذكر عند ذلك قول موسى للخضر -
عليهما  السلام: (أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها، لقد جئت شيئا إمرا) ، وكونه مخطئا في
إنكاره اعتمادا على الظاهر.

### | آداب الولد مع الوالدين

وإن كان لك والدان، فآداب الولد مع الوالدين: أن يسمع كلامهما، ويقوم
لقيامهما؛ ويمتثل لأمرهما، ولا يمشي أمامهما، ولا يرفع صوته فوق
أصواتهما، ويلبي دعوتهما، ويحرص على مرضاتهما، ويخفض لهما جناح الذل، ولا
يمن عليهما بالبر لهما ولا بالقيام لأمرهما، ولا ينظر إليهما شذرا، ولا
يقطب وجهه في وجههما، ولا يسافر إلا بإذنهما.

### | أصناف الناس في العلاقة بالمرء

واعلم أن الناس بعد هؤلاء في حقك ثلاثة أصناف: إما أصدقاء، وإما معاريف،
وإما مجاهيل.

### | آداب العلاقة بالعوام المجهولين

فإن بليت بالعوام المجهولين، فآداب مجالستهم: ترك الخوض في حديثهم، وقلة
الإصغاء إلى أراجيفهم، والتغافل عما يجري من سوء ألفاظهم، والاحتراز عن
كثرة لقائهم والحاجة إليهم، والتنبيه على منكراتهم باللطف والنصح عند رجال
القبول منهم.

### | آداب العلاقة بالاخوان والأصدقاء

وأما الإخوان والاصدقاء فعليك فيهم وظيفتان: الوظيفة الأولى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Companionship, inseparable association; the companion (ṣāḥib) is one who never parts from you.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, true companionship (ṣuḥbah) with God is perpetual remembrance (dhikr) and intimacy (uns) with Him, transcending physical presence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal companionship implies physical proximity; metaphorical (majāz) companionship with God is through remembrance and heart-attachment, as in the ḥadīth cited.
- Root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Solitude, emptying oneself; seclusion (khalwah) for private communion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khalwah with God is the soul's withdrawal from creation to attend solely to the Creator — a prerequisite for sincere devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal emptiness of place vs. metaphorical emptying of the heart from worldly concerns.
- Root: أ-د-ب (ʾ-d-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Refinement, discipline, proper conduct; the cultivation of noble traits.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Adab is the practical embodiment of knowledge (ʿilm) in action — the outward form of inward virtue.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: training animals; metaphorical: disciplining the soul to virtuous conduct.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Imperative Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jazāʾ) — The repeated conditional clauses (e.g., "If you are a scholar...", "If you are a student...") establish a juridical-ethical framework where the protasis defines the subject's state and the apodosis prescribes binding duties.
chapters.translation:
I say — Know that your companion who never parts from you in your presence or your travels, in your sleep or your wakefulness — nay, in your life and your death — is your Lord, your Master, your Patron, and your Creator. Whenever you remember Him, He is your intimate companion; for God Most High has said: {«أنا جليس من ذكرين»} ("I am the companion of whoever remembers Me").

And whenever your heart is broken with sorrow over your shortcomings in the due observance of your religion, He is your companion and your constant attendant; for God Most High has said: {«أنا عند المنكسرة قلوبهم من أجلي»} ("I am with those whose hearts are broken for My sake").

Were you to know Him with true knowledge, you would take Him as your companion and set aside all people. But if you cannot attain to that in all your moments, then beware lest you leave your night and your day devoid of a time in which you seclude yourself with your Master and delight with Him in your intimate converse with Him. And at that point, it is incumbent upon you to learn the etiquette of companionship with God Most High.

Its etiquettes are: bowing the head, lowering the gaze, gathering one's concern, constant silence, stillness of the limbs, hastening to the command, avoiding the prohibition, refraining from objection to the divine decree, constant remembrance (dhikr), persevering reflection (fikr), preferring truth over falsehood, despairing of creatures, humility under awe, brokenness under the water, and ceasing from the stratagems of acquisition — trusting in the divine guarantee, relying on God's bounty, and knowing the excellence of His choice.

All of this ought to be your distinguishing mark throughout your night and your day; for these are the etiquettes of companionship with a Companion who never parts from you — whereas all creatures part from you at certain times.

### | The Etiquettes of the Scholar

And if you are a scholar, then the etiquettes of the scholar are: forbearance, adherence to clemency, sitting with gravity in the manner of dignity with bowed head, refraining from arrogance toward all servants — except toward tyrants, as a deterrent to them from oppression — preferring humility in assemblies and gatherings, abandoning jest and frivolity, gentleness with the student, patience with the arrogant one, rectifying the dull-witted through excellent guidance, refraining from harshness toward him, and refraining from pride in saying "I do not know." And [the scholar must] direct his concern to the questioner, comprehend his question, accept the proof, submit to the truth, and return to it when he errs. He must prevent the student from any knowledge that harms him, and restrain him from seeking by beneficial knowledge anything other than the Face of God Most High. And he must deter the student from occupying himself with a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah) before completing his personal obligation (farḍ ʿayn). And the student's personal obligation is to rectify his outward and inward states through piety (taqwā) — and the scholar must first call his own soul to account in piety, so that the student first learns from his deeds, and secondly benefits from his words.

### | The Etiquettes of the Student

And if you are a student, then the etiquettes of the student with the scholar are: that he begin with greeting and salutation; that he speak little in his presence; that he not speak unless his master asks him; that he not ask until he has first sought permission; that he not say in opposition to his statement, "So-and-so said contrary to what you have said"; that he not indicate to him a view contrary to his opinion, such that he deems himself more knowledgeable of what is correct than his master; that he not question his companion in his master's session; that he not glance about to the sides, but rather sit with bowed head, still, well-mannered, as if in prayer; that he not multiply questions upon him when he is weary; that when he rises, he rise for him; that he not follow him with his speech and questioning; that he not ask him on his way until he reaches his home; and that he not think ill of him regarding actions whose outward appearance seems objectionable to him — for he knows better the secrets thereof. Let him recall at that point the saying of Moses to al-Khiḍr — peace be upon them both: {«أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها، لقد جئت شيئا إمرا»} ("Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have indeed committed a grievous thing") — and that Moses was mistaken in his objection, having relied upon the outward appearance.

### | The Etiquettes of the Child with Parents

And if you have parents, then the etiquettes of the child with them are: that he listen to their words, rise when they rise, comply with their commands, not walk before them, not raise his voice above theirs, respond to their call, be eager for their pleasure, lower to them the wing of humility, not reproach them for his dutifulness to them nor for his service to their affairs, not look at them with aversion, not frown in their faces, and not travel except with their permission.

### | The Categories of People in Relation to a Person

And know that people after these, in relation to you, are of three categories: either friends, or acquaintances, or strangers.

### | The Etiquettes of Relations with the Common Strangers

If you are afflicted with the common strangers, then the etiquettes of sitting with them are: refraining from plunging into their discourse, paying little heed to their rumors, overlooking whatever occurs of their foul speech, guarding against frequent meetings with them and need of them, and admonishing them of their wrongdoings with gentleness and sincere counsel — among those of them who are receptive.

### | شروط الصحبة والصداقة

إحداهما: أن تطلب أولا شروط الصحبة والصداقة، فلا تؤاخ إلا من يصلح
للاخوة والصداقة، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (المرء على دين خليله
فلينظر أحدكم من يخالل) .
فإذا طلبت رفيقا ليكون شريكك في التعلم، وصاحبك في أمر دينك ودنياك، فراع
فيه خمس خصال: الأولى: العقل: فلا خير في صحبة الأحمق، فإلى الوحشة
والقطيعة يرجع آخرها، وأحسن أحواله أن يضرك وهو يريد أن ينفعك، والعدو
العاقل خير من الصديق الأحمق، قال علي رضي الله عنه:
فلا تصحب أخا الجهل ... وإياك وإياه
فكم من جاهل أردى ... حليما حين آخاه
يقاس المرء بالمرء ... إذا ما المرء ماشاه
كحذو النعل بالنعل ... إذا مالنعل حاذاه
وللشىء من الشىء ... مقاييس وأشباه
وللقلب على القلب ... دليل حين يلقاه
الثانية: حسن الخلق: فلا تصحب من ساء خلقه، وهو الذي لا يملك نفسه عند
الغضب والشهوة. وقد جمعه علقمة العطاردي رحمه الله تعالى في وصيته لابنه
لما حضرته الوفاة، قال: يا بني إذا أردت صحبة إنسان فاصحب من إذا خدمته
صانك،  وإن صحبته زانك، وإن قعدت بك مؤنة مانك.. اصحب من إذا مددت يدك بخير
مدها، وإن رأى منك حسنة عدها، وإن رأى منك سيئة سدها.
اصحب من إذا قلت صدق قولك، وإن حاولت أمرا أمرك، وإن تنازعتما في شر
آثرك.
وقال علي رضي الله عنه رجزا:
إن أخاك الحق من كان معك ... ومن يضر نفسه لينفعك
ومن إذا ريب الزمان صدعك ... شتت فيك شمله ليجمعك
الثالثة: الصلاح: فلا تصحب فاسقا مصرا على معصية كبيرة، لأن من يخاف الله
لا يصر على كبيرة، ومن لا يخاف الله لا تؤمن غوائله، بل يتغير بتغير
الأحوال والأعراض، قال الله تعالى لنبيه
صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان
أمره فرطا) .
فاحذر صحبة الفاسق؛ فإن مشاهدة الفسق والمعصية على الدوام تزيل عن قلبك
كراهية المعصية، وتهون عليك أمرها، ولذلك هان على القلوب معصية الغيبة
لإلفهم لها، ولو رأو خاتما من ذهب أو ملبوسا من حرير على فقيه لاشتد
إنكارهم عليه، والغيبة أشد من ذلك.
الرابعة: ألا يكون حريصا على الدنيا: فصحبة الحريص على الدنيا سم قاتل؛
لأن الطباع مجبولة على التشبه والاقتداء، بل الطبع يسرق من الطبع من حيث لا
يدري فمجالسه الحريص تزيد في حرصك، ومجالسه الزاهد تزيد في زهدك.
الخامسة: الصدق: فلا تصحب كذابا، فإنك منه على غرور، فإنه مثل السراب،
يقرب منك البعيد، ويبعد منك القريب.
ولعلك تعدم اجتماع هذه الخصال في سكان المدارس والمساجد، فعليك بأحد
أمرين: إما العزلة والانفراد؛ ففيها سلامتك.. وإما أن تكون مخالطتك مع
شركائك بقدر خصالهم، بأن تعلم أن الاخوة ثلاثة: أخ لآخرين فلا تراع فيه إلا
الدين، وأخ لدنياك فلا تراع فيه إلا الخلق الحسن، وأخ لتأنس به فلا تراع
فيه إلا السلامة من شره وفتنته وخبثه.
والناس ثلاثة: أحدهم مثله مثل الغذاء لا يستغنى عنه، والآخر مثله مثل
الدواء يحتاج إليه في وقت دون وقت، والثالث مثله مثل الداء لا يحتاج إليه
قط، ولكن العبد قد يتسلى  به، وهو الذي لا أنس فيه ولا نفع؛ فتجب مداراته
إلى الخلاص منه، وفي مشاهدته فائدة عظيمة إن وفقت لها، وهو أن تشاهد من
خبائث أحواله وأفعاله ما تستقبحه فتجتنبه؛ فالسعيد من وعظ بغيره، والمؤمن
مرآة المؤمن، وقيل لعيسى عليه السلام: من أدبك؟ فقال: ما أدبني أحد، ولكن
رأيت جهل الجاهل فاجتنبته. ولقد صدق - على نبينا وعليه الصلاة والسلام -
فلو اجتنب الناس ما يكرهونه من غيرهم لكملت آدابهم واستغنوا عن المؤدبين.

  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): True friendship as spiritual interpenetration affecting one's religious state (dīn)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical interstices; metaphorical for intimate companionship that shapes character

chapters.translation:
I say: Know that companionship and friendship have conditions which must be observed.

One of them is that you should first seek out the conditions of companionship and friendship, and not take as a brother anyone except one who is fit for brotherhood and friendship. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«المرء على دين خليله فلينظر أحدكم من يخالل»} ("A man follows the religion of his intimate friend, so let each of you consider whom he takes as an intimate friend").

So when you seek a companion to be your partner in learning and your associate in the affairs of your religion and your worldly life, then observe in him five qualities:

The first: intelligence (ʿaql). For there is no good in the companionship of a fool; its end returns to estrangement and severance, and the best of his states is that he harms you while intending to benefit you. An intelligent enemy is better than a foolish friend. ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said in verse:

"Do not accompany the brother of ignorance — and beware of him entirely!
For how many an ignorant man has ruined a prudent man when he took him as a brother!
A man is measured by a man when a man walks with him,
Like the fitting of a sandal to a sandal when the sandal matches it.
And for a thing there are from a thing measures and likenesses,
And for the heart there is upon the heart an evidence when it encounters it."

The second: good character (ḥusn al-khuluq). Do not accompany one whose character is evil — that is, one who does not possess his own soul at the time of anger and lust. Alqamah al-ʿAṭāridī, may God Most High have mercy on him, gathered this in his testament to his son when death was present before him. He said: "O my son, if you wish to accompany a person, then accompany one who, when you serve him, protects you; and if you accompany him, adorns you; and if a burden befalls you, sustains you. Accompany one who, when you extend your hand with good, extends his; and if he sees from you a good deed, counts it; and if he sees from you an evil deed, conceals it. Accompany one who, when you speak, affirms your speech; and when you attempt a matter, commands you to it; and when you two dispute over something evil, prefers you over himself."

And ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said in rajaz meter:

"Indeed your true brother is he who stands with you — and who harms himself to benefit you,
And who, when the vicissitudes of time rend you, scatters his own affairs to gather you together."

The third: righteousness (ṣalāḥ). Do not accompany a corrupt person (fāsiq) who persists in a major sin. For whoever fears God does not persist in a major sin, and whoever does not fear God, his destructive evils are not safe from — rather, he changes with the changing of circumstances and accidents. God Most High said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: {«ولا تطع من أغفلنا قلبه عن ذكرنا واتبع هواه وكان أمره فرطا»} ("And do not obey him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, and who follows his desire, and whose affair is excess").

So beware of the companionship of a corrupt person; for the constant witnessing of corruption and disobedience removes from your heart the aversion to disobedience, and makes its matter light upon you. For this reason, the sin of backbiting (ghībah) has become light upon hearts because of their familiarity with it. Had they seen a ring of gold or a garment of silk upon a jurist, their disapproval of him would be intense — yet backbiting is more severe than that.

The fourth: that he not be greedy for the worldly life (ḥarīṣ ʿalā al-dunyā). For the companionship of one greedy for the world is a deadly poison; because natures are instinctively disposed to imitation and emulation — indeed, the nature steals from the nature without awareness. So sitting with the greedy increases your greed, and sitting with the ascetic (zāhid) increases your asceticism.

The fifth: truthfulness (ṣidq). Do not accompany a liar, for you are in deception with him. He is like a mirage (sarāb): he brings near to you what is far, and distances from you what is near.

Perhaps you will find the gathering of all these qualities lacking among the inhabitants of schools and mosques. Then you must do one of two things: either seclusion (ʿuzlah) and solitude — for in it is your safety — or your mixing with your associates should be proportionate to their qualities. That is, you should know that brotherhood is of three kinds: a brother for the sake of the Hereafter — then observe in him only religion; a brother for your worldly life — then observe in him only good character; and a brother for companionship and comfort — then observe in him only safety from his evil, his tribulation, and his malice.

And people are of three kinds: one of them is like food — indispensable; another is like medicine — needed at one time and not another; and the third is like disease — never needed at all. But the servant may seek diversion with him — and he is the one in whom there is neither comfort nor benefit. So it is obligatory to manage him tactfully (mudārāh) until one is delivered from him. And in observing him there is a great benefit, if you are granted success in it: namely, that you witness from his vile states and deeds what you deem repugnant, and so you avoid it. For the fortunate one is he who is admonished by others, and the believer is the mirror of the believer. And it was said to Jesus, peace be upon him: "Who taught you adab (refinement)?" He said: "No one taught me, but I saw the ignorance of the ignorant and avoided it." And he spoke truly — upon our Prophet and upon him be prayer and peace. For if people avoided what they dislike in others, their refinements would be perfected and they would have no need of teachers of adab.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الوظيفة الثانية

مراعاة حقوق الصحبة
فمهما انعقدت الشركة، وانتظمت بينك وبين شريكك الصحبة، فعليك حقوق يوجبها
عقد الصحبة، وفي القيام بها آداب، وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (مثل
الأخوين مثل اليدين تغسل إحداهما الأخرى) ، ودخل صلى الله عليه وسلم
أجدمعة، فاجتنى منها سواكين، أحدهما معوج، والآخر مستقيم، وكان معه بعض
أصحابه، فأعطاه المستقيم، وأمسك لنفسه المعوج، فقال: يارسول الله أنت أحق
مني بالمستقيم، فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ما من صاحب يصحب صاحبا ولو ساعة
من نهار إلا وسئل عن صحبته، هل أقام فيها حق الله تعالى أو أضاعه) . وقال
صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ما اصطحب اثنان قط إلا وكان أحبهما إلى الله تعالى
أرفقهما بصاحبه) .
وآداب الصحبة: الايثار بالمال، فإن لم يكن هذا فبذل الفضل من المال عند
الحاجة، والإعانة بالنفس في الحاجات، على سبيل المبادرة من غير احواج إلى
التماس، وكتمان السر، وستر العيوب، والسكوت على تبليغ ما يسوؤه من مذمة
الناس إياه، وإبلاغ ما يسره من ثناء الناس عليه، وحسن الإصغاء عند الحديث،
وترك المماراة فيه، وأن يدعوه بأحب أسمائه إليهس، وأن ثني عليه بما يعرف من
محاسنه، وأن يشكره على صنيعه في وجهه، وأن يذب عنه في غيبته إذا تعرض لعرضه
كما يذب عن نفسه، وأن ينصحه باللطف والتعريض إذا احتاج إليه، وأن يعفو عن
زلته وهفوته، ولا يعتب عليه، وأن يدعو له في خلوته في حياته وبعد مماته،
وأن يحسن الوفاء مع أهله وأقاربه بعد موته، وأن يؤثر التخفيف عنه، فلا
يكلفه شيئا  من حاجاه، فيروح سره من مهماته، وأن يظهر الفرح بجميع ما يرتاح
له من مساره، والحزن على نياله من مكارهه، وأن يضمر في قلبه مثل ما يظهره،
فيكون صادقا في وده سرا وعلانية، وأن يبدأه بالسلام عند إقباله، وأن يوسع
له في المجلس ويخرج له من مكانه، وأن يشيعه عند قيامه، وأن يصمت عند كلامه
حتى يفرغ من كلامه، ويترك المداحلة في كلامه. وعلى الجملة، فيعامله بما يحب
أن يعامل به، فمن لا يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه فأخوته نفاق، وهي عليه وبال في
الدنيا والآخرة.
فهذا أدبك في حق العوام المجهولين، وف يحق الأصدقاء المؤاخين.

### | آداب العلاقة بالمعارف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes association, accompaniment, and enduring presence alongside another; a companion (ṣāḥib) is one who is never parted from you in intimacy or need.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ṣuḥbah signifies a covenant of mutual obligation mirroring the believer’s companionship with Allah—demanding fidelity (wafāʾ) and selflessness (īthār).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical accompaniment; metaphorical (majāz) = spiritual and moral alliance where rights (ḥuqūq) bind the heart, not merely the body.
- Root: أ-ث-ر (a-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Preference, choosing one thing over another; īthār is the act of giving precedence to another’s need over one’s own desire.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Īthār is the peak of moral excellence (muruwwah)—preferring the brother’s benefit even at personal cost, a trait of the truthful (ṣiddīqūn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = selecting; metaphorical = voluntary self-deprivation for the other’s sake, as in the Quranic praise of the Anṣār.
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To erase, pardon, leave unpunished; ʿafw implies wiping away the fault entirely without residue of resentment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAfw is the divine and human virtue of overlooking slips (zallāt) as an act of magnanimity, distinct from mere forbearance (ḥilm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = obliteration of a trace; metaphorical = pardoning a wrong so completely that no blame (ʿitāb) remains.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inna-mā (إنما) — The particle restricts the predicate to the subject, emphasizing that companionship’s essence is defined solely by the fulfillment of divine rights, as in the Hadith’s conditional interrogation (saʾala ʿan ṣuḥbatihi).
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the second duty is the observance of the rights of companionship. Whenever the bond of partnership is forged, and companionship is woven between you and your fellow, then upon you are rights that the covenant of companionship necessitates, and in fulfilling them there are etiquettes. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«مثل الأخوين مثل اليدين تغسل إحداهما الأخرى»} — “The likeness of two brothers is the likeness of two hands, one washing the other.” And he, peace and blessings be upon him, entered a garden, and plucked from it two tooth-sticks (siwāk), one crooked and the other straight, while one of his companions was with him. He gave the straight one to him and kept the crooked one for himself. The companion said: “O Messenger of Allah, you are more deserving of the straight one than I.” He, peace and blessings be upon him, replied: {«ما من صاحب يصحب صاحبا ولو ساعة من نهار إلا وسئل عن صحبته، هل أقام فيها حق الله تعالى أو أضاعه»} — “There is no companion who accompanies another, even for an hour of the day, but he will be asked about his companionship: did he uphold therein the right of Allah, exalted is He, or did he squander it?” And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«ما اصطحب اثنان قط إلا وكان أحبهما إلى الله تعالى أرفقهما بصاحبه»} — “Two have never companioned each other but that the more beloved of them to Allah, exalted is He, was the more gentle (arfaq) of them to his companion.”

The etiquettes of companionship are: preferring the other in wealth (īthār bil-māl) — and if this is not possible, then expending the surplus of wealth at the time of need; aiding with one’s own person in necessities, hastening to do so without being asked; concealing secrets; veiling faults; remaining silent upon hearing what grieves him of people’s censure against him; conveying what delights him of people’s praise upon him; listening well when he speaks; abandoning contentious argument (mumārāh) in his speech; calling him by the most beloved of his names to him; praising him for the virtues known of him; thanking him for his deed to his face; defending him in his absence when his honor is assailed, just as one defends one’s own honor; advising him with gentleness and indirect allusion (taʿrīḍ) when he needs it; pardoning his slip (zallat) and his error (hafwah), without reproaching him; supplicating for him in private, in his life and after his death; fulfilling well (ḥusn al-wafāʾ) toward his family and kin after his passing; preferring to lighten his burden, so that you do not impose upon him any of your needs, thus granting his heart relief from his cares; showing joy at all that delights him of his pleasures, and grief at what befalls him of his adversities; and harboring in your heart the like of what you show outwardly, so that you are truthful in your affection (wudd) in secret and in public; greeting him with salām when he approaches; making space for him in the gathering and yielding your place to him; accompanying him when he rises; falling silent while he speaks until he finishes his speech; and refraining from deceitful maneuvering (mudāhalah) in his discourse. In sum, treat him as you would love to be treated. For whoever does not love for his brother what he loves for himself, his brotherhood is hypocrisy (nifāq), and it is a burden (wabāl) upon him in this world and the Hereafter.

This, then, is your etiquette toward the common folk who are unknown to you, and toward friends who are sworn brothers.

### | Etiquettes of Relations with Acquaintances

chapters.title_en: On Acquaintances, Their Dangers, and the Etiquette of Social Conduct
chapters.arabic_text:
وأما القسم الثالث، وهم المعارف: فاحذر منهم؛ فإنك لا تر الشر إلا ممن
تعرفه، أم الصديق فيعينك، وأما المجهول فلا يتعرض لك، وإنما الشر كله من
المعارف الذين يظهرون الصداقة بألسنتهم.
فأقلل من المعارف ما قدرت، فإذا بليت بهم في مدرسة أو مسجد أو جامع أو
سوق أو بلد، فيجب ألا تستصغر منهم أحدا؛ فإنك لا تدري لعله خير منك، ولا
تنظر إليهم بعين التعظيم لهم في
حال دنياهم فتهلك، لأن الدنيا صغيرة عند الله تعالى، صغير ما فيها. ومهما
عظم أهل الدنيا في قلبك فقد سقطت من عين الله تعالى، وإياك أن تبذل لهم
دينك لتنال به من دنياهم؛ فلا يفعل ذلك أحد إلا صغر في أعينهم ثم حرم ما
عندهم.
وإن عادوك فلا تقابلهم بالعداوة؛ فإنك لا تطيق الصبر على مكافأتهم، فيذهب
دينك في عداوتهم، ويطول عناؤك معهم، ولا تسكن إليهم في حال إكرامهم إياك
وثنائهم عليك في وجهك وإظهارهم المودة لك؛ فإنك إن طلبت حقيقة ذلك لم تجد
في المائة واحدا، ولا تطمع أن يكونوا لك في السر والعلن واحد، ولا تتعجب إن
ثلبوك في غيبتك ولا تغضب منه؛ فإنك إن أنصفت وجدت من نفسك مثل ذلك، حتى في
أصدقائك وأقاربك، بل في أستاذك ووالديك؛ فإنك تذكرهم في الغيبة بما لا
تشافههم به، فاقطع طمعك عن مالهم وجاههم  ومعونتهم؛ فإن الطامع في الأكثر
خائب في المال، وهو ذليل لا محالة في الحال.
وإذا سألت واحدا حاجة فقضاها، فاشكر الله تعالى واشكره، وإن قصر فلا
تعاتبه ولا تشكه فتصير عدواة له، وكن كالمؤمن يطلب المعاذير، ولا تكن
كالمنافق يطلب العيوب، وقل لعله قصر لعذر له لم أطلع عليه.
ولا تعظن أحدا منهم ما لم تتوسم فيه أو مخايل القبول، وإلا لم يستمع منك
وصار خصما عليك، إذا أخطئوا في مسألة، وكانوا يأنفون من التعلم منك، فلا
تعلمهم؛ فلا تعلمهم؛ ن فإنهم يستفيدون منك علما ويصبحون لك أعداء، إلا إذا
تعلق ذلك بمعصية يقارفونها عن جهل منهم، فاذكر الحق بلطف من غير عنف.
وإذا رأيت منهم كرامة وخيرا، فاشكر الله الذي حببك إليهم. وإذا رأيت منهم
شرا، فكلهم إلى الله تعالى، واستعذ بالله من شرهم، ولا تعاتبهم، ولا تقل
لهم: لم لم تعرفوا حقي؛ وأنا فلان بن فلان، وأنا الفاضل في العلوم؟ فإن ذلك
من كلام الحمقى، وأشد الناس حماقة من يزكي نفسه ويثني عليها.
واعلم أن الله تعالى لا يسلطهم عليك إلا بذنب سبق منك، فاستغفر الله من
ذنبك، واعلم أن ذلك عقوبة من الله تعالى.
وكن فيما بينهم سميعا لحقهم، أصم عن باطلهم، نطوفا بمحاسنهم، صموتا عن
مساويهم، واحذر مخالطة متفقهة الزمان، لا سيما المشتغلين بالخلاف والجدال.
واحذر منهم؛ فإنهم يتربصون بك - لحسدهم - ريب المنون، ويقطعون عليك
بالظنون، ويتغامرون وراءك بالعيون، ويحصون عليك عثراتك في عشرتهم، حتى
يجبهوك بها في حال غيظهم ومناظرتهم، لا يقيلون لك عثرة، ولا يغفرون لك زلة،
ولا يسترون لك
عورة، يحاسبونك على النقير والقطمير، ويحسدونك على القليل والكثير،
ويحرضون عليك الإخوان بالنميمة والبلاغات والبهتان، إن رضوا فظاهرهم الملق،
وإن سخطوا فباطنهم الحنق، ظاهرهم ثياب وباطنهم ذئاب.
هذا ما قطعت به المشاهدة على أكثرهم، إلا من عصمه الله تعالى؛ فصحبتهم
خسران، ومعاشرتهم خذلان.
هذا حكم من يظهر لك الصداقة، فكيف من يجاهرك بالعداوة؟ قال القاضي ابن
معروف رحمه الله تعالى:
فاحذر عدوك مرة ... واحذر  صديقك ألف مرة
فلربما انقلب الصديق ... فكان اعرف بالمضرة
وكذلك قال أبو تمام:
عدوك من صديقك مستفاد ... فلا تستكثرن من الصحاب
فإن الداء أكثر ما تراه ... يكون من الطعام أو الشراب
وكن كما قال هلال بن العلاء الرقى:
لما عفوت ولم أحقد على أحد ... أرحت نفسى من هم العداوات
إني أحيى عدوى عند رؤيته ... لأدفع الشر عنى بالتحيات
وأظهر البشر للإنسان أبغضه ... كأن قد ملا قلبى مرات
ولست أسلم ممن لست أعرفه ... فكيف أسلم من أهل المودات
الناس داء دواء الناس تركهم ... وفي الجفاء لهم قطع الأخوات
فسالم الناس تسلم من غوائلهم ... وكن حريصا على كسب التقيات
وخالق الناس واصبر ما بليت بهم ... اصم ابكم اعمى ذا تقيات
وكن أيضا كما قال بعض الحكماء: الق صديقك وعدوك بوجه الرضا، من غير مذلة
لهما ولا هيبة منهما، وتوقر من غير كبر، وتواضع من غير مذلة، وكن في جميع
أمورك في أوسطها، فكلا طرفى قصدن الأمور ذميم، كما قيل:
عليك بأوساط الأمور فإنها ... طريق إلى نهج الصراط قويم
ولا تك فيها مفرطا أو مفرطا ... فإن كلا حال الأمور ذميم
ولا تنظر في عطفيك، ولا تكثر إلى وارئك الالتفات، ولا تقف على الجماعات،
وإذا جلست فلا تستوفز، وتحفظ من تشبيك أصابعك، وكثرة بصاقك ونخمك، وطر
الذباب عن وجهك، وكثرة التمطى والتثاؤب في وجوه الناس في الصلاة وغيرها،
وليكن مجلسك هادئا، وحديثك منظوما مرتبا، واصغ إلى الكلام الحسن ممن حدثك
من غير إظهار تعجب مفرط، ولا تسأله إعادته، واسكت عن المضاحك والحكايات،
ولا تحدث عن إعجابك بولدك وشعرك وكلامك وتصنيفك وسائر ما يخصك، ولا تتصنع
تصنع المرأة في التزين، ولا تتبذل تبذل العبد، وتوق كثرة الكحل والإسراف
في الدهن، ولا تلح في الحاجات، ولا تشجع أحدا على الظلم، ولا تعلم أحدا
من أهلك وولدك فضلا عن غيرهم مقدار مالك؛ واجفهم من غير عنف، ولن لهم من
غير ضعف، ولا تهازل أمتك ولا عبدك، فيسقط وقارك من قلوبهم، وإذا خاصمت
فتوقر، وتحفئ من جهلك وعجلتك،  وتفكر في حجتك، ولا تكثر الاشارة بيدك، ولا
تكثر الالتفاف إلى من ورائك ولا تجث على ركبتيك، وإذا هدأ غضبك فتكلم. وإذا
قربك السلطان فكن منه على حد السنان، وإياك وصديق العافية؛ فإنه أعدى
الأعداء، ولا يجعل مالك أكرم من عرضك.
فهذا القدر يافتى يكفيك من بداية الهداية، فجرب بها نفسك؛ فإنها ثلاثة
أقسام: قسم آداب الطاعات، وقسم في ترك المعاصي، وقسم في مخالطة الخلق، وهي
جامعة لجمل معاملة العبد مع الخالق والخلق.
فإن رأيتها مناسبة لنفسك، ورأيت قلبك مائلا إليها راغبا في العمل بها،
فاعلم أنك عبد نور الله تعالى بالإيمان قلبك، وشرح به صدرك، وتحقق أن لهذه
البداية نهاية، ووراءها أسرارا وأغوارا ومكاشفات، وقد أودعناها كتاب (إحياء
علوم الدين) ؛ فاشتغل بتحصيله.
وإن رأيت نفسك تستثقل العمل بهذه الوظائف، وتنكر هذا الفن من العلم،
وتقول لك نفسك: أنى ينفعك هذا العلم في محافل العلماء، ومتى يقدمك هذا على
الأقران والنظراء؟! وكيف يرفع منصبك في مجالس الأمراء والوزراء؟ وكيف يوصلك
إلى الصلة والأرزاق وولاية الأوقاف والقضاء؟ فاعلم أن الشيطان قد أغواك
وأنساك متقلبك ومثواك، فاطلب لك شيطانا مثلك، ليعملك ما تظن أنه ينفعك
ويوصلك إلى بغيتك. ثم أنه قط لا يصفو لك الملك في محلتك، فضلا عن قريتك
وبلدتك، ثم يفوتك الملك المقيم والنعيم الدائم في جوار رب العالمين.
والسلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، والحمد لله أولا وآخرا، وظاهرا
وباطنا. ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم. وصلى الله على سيدنا محمد
وآله وصحبه، وسلم تسليما كثيرا. PageV01P070
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع ر ف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge by experience or perception; recognition of a thing through its traces; acquaintance (maʿrifah) as opposed to mere knowledge (ʿilm).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Maʿrifah denotes a cognition that follows reflection and discernment of distinguishing marks; in social context, it implies familiarity that breeds expectation and vulnerability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is recognition; metaphorically extended to social intimacy, where the "known one" (maʿrif) is one whose presence is familiar—hence, one whose harm is more feared than the stranger's.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Adversative Coordination (al-ʿAṭf bi-lākin) — The text repeatedly pivots with "أما... فأ..." (as for... then...), establishing contrastive parallelism that governs the syntactic rhythm of admonition.
chapters.translation:
As for the third category—the acquaintances—beware of them! For you will never see evil except from one whom you know. As for the sincere friend, he aids you; and as for the unknown, he does not molest you. Rather, all evil comes entirely from acquaintances who display friendship with their tongues.

So minimize your acquaintances as much as you are able. And when you are afflicted with them—in a school, a mosque, a congregational mosque, a market, or a town—then it is incumbent upon you not to deem any of them insignificant, for you do not know; perhaps he is better than you. And do not look upon them with an eye of veneration for them in their worldly state, lest you perish—for the world is small in the sight of God (Exalted is He), and small is whatever is in it. And whenever the people of the world become great in your heart, you have fallen from the sight of God (Exalted is He). And beware of bartering your religion for them to attain thereby some of their worldly goods; for none does this except that he becomes small in their eyes, then is deprived of what they possess.

And if they show enmity toward you, do not meet them with enmity; for you cannot endure the strain of requiting them, and so your religion would be wasted in their enmity, and your toil would be prolonged with them. And do not repose in them when they honor you, praise you to your face, and display affection toward you; for if you sought the reality of that, you would not find one in a hundred. And do not hope that they will be the same toward you in secret as in public. And do not be astonished if they defame you in your absence, nor become angry at it; for if you were just, you would find the like of that in yourself—even regarding your friends and relatives, nay, even your teacher and your parents; for you mention them in their absence with what you do not say to their faces. So cut off your hope from their wealth, their status, and their assistance; for the one who hopes for much is disappointed in wealth, and he is humiliated without fail in the present moment.

And if you ask someone for a need and he fulfills it, then thank God (Exalted is He) and thank him. And if he falls short, do not reproach him nor complain of him, lest he become an enemy to you. And be like the believer who seeks excuses, and do not be like the hypocrite who seeks faults. And say: "Perhaps he fell short due to an excuse of which I have not become aware."

And do not admonish any of them unless you discern in him signs of acceptance; otherwise he will not listen to you and will become an adversary against you. And if they err in a matter, and they disdain learning from you, then do not teach them; for they would derive knowledge from you and then become enemies to you—except when it pertains to a disobedience they are committing out of ignorance; then mention the truth gently, without harshness.

And if you see from them honor and goodness, thank God who made you beloved to them. And if you see from them evil, then delegate them to God (Exalted is He), and seek refuge in God from their evil, and do not reproach them, nor say to them: "Why did you not recognize my right? I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and I am the preeminent one in the sciences?" For that is the speech of fools; and the most foolish of people is the one who praises himself and commends himself.

And know that God (Exalted is He) does not give them power over you except due to a sin that preceded from you. So seek forgiveness from God for your sin, and know that this is a punishment from God (Exalted is He).

And be, among them, one who hears their rights, deaf to their falsehood; one who speaks much of their virtues, silent about their vices. And beware of mixing with the pseudo-jurists (mutafaqqihah) of the age—especially those occupied with disputation (khilāf) and argumentation (jadal). Beware of them! For they—out of envy—lie in wait for you with the vicissitudes of fate, and they pass judgments upon you with suspicions, and they vie behind your back with glances, and they count your slips in their company, until they confront you with them in moments of their rage and their disputations. They do not pardon a slip of yours, nor forgive a lapse, nor conceal a fault. They call you to account over the pittance of a date-stone (al-naqīr) and the husk of a seed (al-qaṭmīr), and they envy you for the little and the much. They incite brothers against you with slander, reports, and calumny. If they are pleased, their outward is flattery; if they are angered, their inward is rancor. Their outward is garments; their inward is wolves.

This is what direct observation (mushāhadah) has affirmed concerning most of them—except those whom God (Exalted is He) has protected. So their companionship is loss, and their association is abandonment.

This is the ruling concerning one who shows you friendship—so how about one who openly declares enmity toward you? The Judge Ibn Maʿrūf (may God have mercy on him) said:

*Beware of your enemy once, and beware of your friend a thousand times; for perhaps the friend turns, and becomes more knowing of harm.*

And likewise Abū Tammām said:

*Your enemy is derived from your friend—so do not multiply companions excessively; for the disease, most often seen, comes from food or drink.*

And be as Hilāl ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-Raqqī said:

*When I forgave and bore no grudge against anyone, I gave my soul rest from the cares of enmities. I greet my enemy when I see him, to ward off evil from me with salutations. And I show cheerfulness to the person I detest, as though my heart were filled with love. And I am not safe from one I do not know—so how can I be safe from those who profess affection? People are a disease; the cure of people is to abandon them, and in aloofness from them lies the severing of bonds. So make peace with people, and you will be safe from their treacheries; and be eager in acquiring acts of piety. And mix with people and be patient when afflicted with them—deaf, mute, blind, possessed of piety.*

And be also as one of the sages said: Meet your friend and your enemy with a face of contentment—without humiliation toward them and without awe of them. And be dignified without pride, and humble without abasement. And be in all your affairs in their middle course; for both extremes of affairs are blameworthy, as it was said:

*Adhere to the middle courses of affairs, for they are a path to the straight road (al-ṣirāṭ). And be not in them excessive or negligent, for indeed both states of affairs are blameworthy.*

And do not glance sideways, and do not frequently turn to look behind you, and do not stand about in crowds. And when you sit, do not sit perched restlessly. And guard against interlacing your fingers, excessive spitting and clearing your throat, brushing flies from your face, and frequent stretching and yawning in people's faces—in prayer and otherwise. And let your sitting be calm, and your speech well-ordered and arranged. And listen attentively to good speech from whoever speaks to you—without displaying excessive astonishment, and without asking him to repeat it. And refrain from jokes and anecdotes. And do not speak out of admiration for your child, your poetry, your speech, your compositions, and all that pertains specifically to you. And do not adorn yourself with the adornment of a woman, nor let yourself go with the slovenliness of a slave. And beware of excessive kohl and extravagance in oil. And do not be importunate in requests. And do not encourage anyone toward injustice. And do not inform anyone of your family and children—let alone others—of the amount of your wealth. And be stern with them without harshness, and gentle with them without weakness. And do not jest with your slave-girl or your slave, lest your dignity fall from their hearts. And when you dispute, be dignified, and restrain yourself from your ignorance and haste, and reflect upon your proof. And do not gesture excessively with your hand, and do not turn frequently to those behind you, and do not kneel upon your knees. And when your anger subsides, then speak. And if the ruler brings you near, then be with him on the edge of the spear-point. And beware of the friend of prosperity (ṣadīq al-ʿāfiyah); for he is the most hostile of enemies. And do not make your wealth more honorable than your honor (ʿirḍ).

This much, O youth, suffices you from the Beginning of Guidance (Bidāyat al-Hidāyah). So test yourself by it; for it consists of three parts: a part on the etiquettes of acts of obedience, a part on abandoning sins, and a part on mixing with creation—and it is comprehensive of the entirety of the servant's conduct with the Creator and with creation.

If you see it as suitable to yourself, and you see your heart inclining toward it and desiring to act upon it, then know that you are a servant whom God (Exalted is He) has illuminated with faith in your heart and expanded your breast thereby. And be certain that this beginning has an end, and beyond it are secrets, depths, and unveilings (mukāshafāt) which we have deposited in the book Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn (The Revival of the Religious Sciences); so occupy yourself with acquiring it.

And if you see your soul deeming these duties burdensome, and denying this art of knowledge, and your soul says to you: "How will this knowledge benefit you in the assemblies of the scholars? And when will this advance you over your peers and contemporaries? And how will it elevate your rank in the councils of princes and viziers? And how will it lead you to gifts, stipends, the administration of endowments (awqāf), and judgeship?"—then know that Satan has seduced you and made you forget your vicissitudes and your final abode. So seek for yourself a devil like yourself, to teach you what you suppose will benefit you and lead you to your goal. Then, verily, sovereignty will never be purified for you in your own district—let alone your village and your town—and then the abiding sovereignty and the everlasting bliss in the neighborhood of the Lord of the Worlds will slip away from you.

And peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. And praise be to God, first and last, outwardly and inwardly. And there is no might and no power except with God, the Exalted, the Magnificent. And may God send blessings upon our master Muḥammad, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. PageV01P070
